properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-23: *"one thing I've noticed a bit is updating progress of development and testing of the graph … I had been using the /capture-session as sort of a way to make sure the graph is being updated, but things are getting through."*

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
⭐⭐ THE SHAPE, AND IT IS NOT A DISCIPLINE PROBLEM: **CAPTURE IS ADDITIVE. NOTHING ANYWHERE ASKS WHAT A SESSION MADE FALSE.**

Every mechanism in the loop adds: capture-intent adds nodes, `record_change` adds an event, capture-session adds what the conversation held, `loop_status` counts what is OWED. Not one asks *which existing assertion did this work just retire?* So a finding that motivated a fix survives the fix, and goes on proposing work already done.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📐 MEASURED ON THIS DESIGN, 2026-08-23

    TemporalFacts                                    274
      basis = measured                               274   (all of them)
      carrying a valid_to                              7   ⇐ 2.6%
      OPEN (no valid_to)                             267
        ...whose SUBJECT has since been CHANGED      200   ⇐ 74%

**The field that closes a fact already exists and is 97% unused.** `valid_to` is declared on TemporalFact, reachable, and essentially never written.

⚠️ BOUND: "has since been CHANGED" is NOT ordered against `valid_from`. A ChangeEvent carries no date of its own — it is placed by AT_EPOCH — so 200 is an UPPER BOUND on staleness candidates, not a count of stale facts. Sharpening it needs epoch sequence compared against `valid_from`, which was not done here.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
🛑 TWO SIGHTINGS, AND THE FIRST HAPPENED IN THE SESSION THAT RECORDED THIS

(1) **THIS SESSION, CAUGHT BY ANTHONY.** Asked where else to optimise, the agent read `fact:the-orientation-reads-cost-ten-seconds-and-the-store-is-not-why` and quoted its numbers as current — `open_questions` at 11.7s, `detect_defects` the hot spot — with the fact's own words *"NOTHING WAS OPTIMISED"* and *"that ratio is the next measurement and it has not been taken."* **All three were false.** PR #290 had taken the measurement AND fixed it: 56 SPOF candidates at 878ms each became 5.08ms for all 56, `detect_structural_defects` 44.5s → 4.43s, `open_questions` 11.7s → **2.95s**. His reply: *"I think we already determined candidate 3."* He was right; the graph said otherwise. `cmp:service`, that fact's subject, has been CHANGED **nine** times since.

(2) **A DIFFERENT PROJECT, ON HIS OTHER MACHINE.** An agent proposed work, he accepted, and on investigating it reported the work was already done. Same shape, different graph, no shared code — which makes this a property of the MODEL rather than of one session's carelessness.

⭐ AND THE SIBLING NODE SAW THIS COMING FROM THE OTHER SIDE. `dec:idea-search-first-fires-without-being-remembered` measured six saves in one session and found **four of six prevented WORK rather than nodes**, calling that "the more expensive thing". Searching-before-proposing and closing-what-you-invalidated are two different fixes for one symptom: *an agent proposes work that is already done.*

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
IDEAS, UNRANKED, each with what it costs

**A. A DETECTOR — `stale_measurement`.** A `basis: measured` TemporalFact with no `valid_to` whose subject has been CHANGED since `valid_from`.
   ⭐ Needs no discipline, which is the whole argument — every other option asks somebody to remember something at the moment they are least likely to.
   ⚠️ **200 findings on day one is a failure mode this project has already lived through**: per-idea, the unreviewed-ideas detector would have fired 115 times the day it shipped and the category was filtered by week's end. This must be ONE aggregate finding at low severity — or it becomes wallpaper, which is dev_storyflow's reason ① for abandoning reflow2 altogether.
   ⚠️ The ordering stays a proxy until ChangeEvents can be placed in time against `valid_from`.

**B. capture-session ASKS THE INVALIDATION QUESTION.** It captures what a session produced; it could also ask what the session made false.
   ⭐ Cheapest by far — a skill edit, no schema, no code. And it is what Anthony was already using this skill to try to achieve.
   ⚠️ It is PULL, and this is precisely the sibling node's finding: the discipline exists in writing and decays anyway. Where the question SHOULD live; not where it will reliably happen.

**C. AN EDGE: ChangeEvent → the finding it ANSWERS.**
   ⭐⭐ **THIS REVERSES A DECISION TAKEN EARLIER THE SAME DAY, AND THE REVERSAL IS THE MOST USEFUL THING HERE.** `ChangeEvent → Decision` was one of five vocabulary candidates and was DECLINED — by this agent, in this session, hours earlier — on the ground that *"I cannot name a computation that would read it."* **Option A is that computation.** A detector reading ANSWERS edges is EXACT where a subject-changed heuristic is a proxy. The decline was correct on the evidence then available and is wrong now; what changed is that a reader appeared.
   ⚠️ Still a new edge type: moves the stamp, owes an upgrade note, worth nothing until something draws it.

**D. ASK AT THE MOMENT OF THE CHANGE.** `record_change` takes an optional "this answers X".
   ⭐ The one moment the author certainly knows; by session end they have forgotten. And it is the sibling node's own option (a)/(b) shape — put the discipline on the TOOL, not in a catalogue.
   ⚠️ Another field on the busiest write in the loop, and dev_storyflow reported write-time friction is exactly what trains agents to route around typed tools.

**E. THE STOP HOOK COUNTS IT.** "You recorded N ChangeEvents and closed 0 findings."
   ⚠️ `loop_nudge.py` CANNOT READ THE GRAPH — the session's server holds the single-writer lock — so it keys only on the op tally, and `valid_to` goes through a generic `create_node` indistinguishable from any other write. Implementable only if closing a finding gets its own NAMED op, which is an argument for C and D over E.

**F. DO NOTHING — a TemporalFact is a dated observation and staleness is the reader's job.**
   ⭐ The honest defence of the status quo: the type is explicitly temporal, `valid_from` says when it was true, and 274 never-expiring facts cost nothing until somebody reads one as current.
   ⚠️ **And that is exactly what happened, twice, today.** The cost is not theoretical and is not paid by the graph — it is paid by the person who accepts a proposal for work already done.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════
📌 WHAT THIS IS NOT

It is NOT about agents failing to use skills — that is `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session`, accepted, with three observations of its own. A session that used every skill perfectly would still leave this gap. The two failures compound and are independent.
properties.name: OPEN — capture is ADDITIVE and nothing asks what a session made FALSE. 267 measured facts stand open; 200 describe a node that has since moved
properties.rationale:
Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`. Anthony, 2026-08-23, from two independent sightings — one in this session, one on his other machine. Nothing here is intent and nothing is planned.

DEDUP: read six near-matches in full.
· ⭐ `dec:idea-search-first-fires-without-being-remembered` is the SIBLING and the closest of the six. Same shape — a discipline that is written down and still depends on somebody remembering it — and plausibly the same parent, `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue` (proposed, unbuilt), of which this would be a SECOND instance. **But it is a different discipline: that one prevents a duplicate on the way IN, this one closes a finding on the way OUT.** Its own sharpest measurement — *"four of six saves prevented WORK, not nodes"* — is the same symptom this node measures from the other side, which is why it is linked rather than merged.
· `req:skill-use-survives-a-long-session` and `fact:an-agent-stopped-reaching-...` are about agents not REACHING for the loop. **A session that used every skill perfectly would still leave this gap, because no skill asks the invalidation question.**
· `req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause` (ACCEPTED) asks whether a repair reached the CAUSE — a property of the fix. This asks whether it RETIRED THE FINDING — a relation between two records.
· `dec:the-patch-record-binds-forward-not-backward` settles that 472 existing changes are not reclassified; the same courtesy would be owed to the 267 open facts.
· `dec:idea-how-do-triage-findings-become-plannable-work` asks how a finding becomes SCHEDULABLE; this asks how it becomes CLOSED.
